scope: Inventory of production source under hooks/ and skills/*/scripts/. Test references identify registered checks, not evidence that they ran or that every behavior is covered. Enforcement describes the implementation boundary; it does not activate an adapter or establish host acceptance.

entries.limits: Explicit rules migration utility; backups and boundary checks do not authorize migration or establish host installation.
Bounded rule discovery and context assembly; instructions do not enforce subsequent agent actions.
Emits session and repository context when the host invokes the hook; no task execution or host-installation guarantee.
Suggests registered skills from prompt signals; routing text is not an execution gate.
Shared hook context and output helpers; no independent runtime supervision.
Discovers local tool metadata within scan bounds; inventory is not tool availability or successful invocation evidence.
Windows command-lifetime helper used by the update checker; only owns its launched process tree, not general host tasks.
Reports update information when invoked; does not install updates or verify all host integrations.
PowerShell entry point for the update checker; wrapper checks do not prove live registry/network availability.
Explicit Windows C# build helper; source inclusion or test registration does not prove a built binary or active supervisor.
Canonical snapshots and digests validate represented data; they do not prove the truth of runtime observations.
Validates collaboration artifact structure and cross-field contracts; accepted artifacts do not activate a platform adapter.
Checks retry and failure-loop state for callers using this library; cannot gate bypassing callers or host-wide work.
Validates identity and support claims; validation alone does not observe an operating-system process or establish cleanup authority.
Recovery persistence for explicit callers; stored records do not establish external side effects or universal crash recovery.
Library-level admission and state checks only; no automatic host task interception or completed production adapter implied.
Checks modeled transitions; a valid transition is not evidence that an external action occurred.
Finite manager API requires caller-supplied adapter, identity and authorization; synthetic tests do not establish a deployed production adapter.
Tracks registered resources and close evidence for explicit callers; unregistered resources and unsupported hosts remain outside its scope.
Windows Job Object supervisor for explicitly launched children; registration does not prove compilation, installation, active use or non-Windows support.
CLI artifact validation only; a successful contract check does not execute a plan or certify runtime outcomes.
Read-only source, package-declaration, link and registration checks; no behavioral coverage measurement, native compilation or host acceptance.
